pr_title: Avoid infinite loop in recursive type hierarchies
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/112072

We have a somewhat high bar for adding error detection to the builder classes, but this one causes an infinite loop.
pr_comments:
> We have a somewhat high bar for adding error detection to the builder classes, but this one causes an infinite loop.

I think it is one of many situations that can introduce infinite loop in Ref.Emit. Are we going to fix all of them as they are found?
If we end up fixing this, Mono and persisted Reflection.Emit should get the same fix.
Closing; I don't think this is worth pursuing.

issue_context.title: `TypeBuilder.CreateType()` gets stuck in infinite loop when creating a type that has itsself as parent
issue_context.body:
### Description

When the `CreateType()` method is called on a `TypeBuilder` instance, which has set itsself as parent, it will search indefinietely for the top-most parent and will get stuck in a loop.

Although this is a user error it should still throw an exception when trying to call the `SetParent` method with the argument pointing to `this`.

### Reproduction Steps

Consider the following C# Code.

```csharp
void Main()
{
	AssemblyBuilder assemblyCreator = AssemblyBuilder.DefineDynamicAssembly(new AssemblyName("TestAssembly"), AssemblyBuilderAccess.Run);
	
	ModuleBuilder moduleBuilder = assemblyCreator.DefineDynamicModule("TestModule");
	
	TypeBuilder typeBuilder = moduleBuilder.DefineType("TestType", TypeAttributes.Class | TypeAttributes.Public);
	
	typeBuilder.SetParent(typeBuilder);
	
	typeBuilder.CreateType();
}

```

The example creates a new type `TestType` in the dynamic module `TestModule` in the assembly `TestAssembly`. It sets itsself as a parent. Upon calling `typeBuilder.CreateType();`

### Expected behavior

My suggestion is to not let `typeBuilder.SetParent` set itsself so, that a recursion would occur.

### Actual behavior

The application gets stuck in an infinite loop.

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

- .NET 9.0.0
- x64

### Other information

_No response_

The problem is this while loop here:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/e51af404d1ea26be4a3d8e51fe21cf2f09ad34dd/src/coreclr/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Reflection/Emit/RuntimeTypeBuilder.cs#L946-L952

Adding something like this
```csharp
     if (IsTypeEqual(p, this)) 
         throw new Exception( // ...
```
should fix the problem.
Based on feedback from the PR above, and that we normally don't add non-trivial validation to the builder classes, closing.

review_comments:
I think it would be better to just return `false` instead of throwing ArgumentException.

ArgumentException would be fine to throw from SetParent, but that has its own set of problems (it would be a breaking change).

[nitpick] Consider updating the comment to 'if the runtime type view is equal, then the types are considered equal' for better clarity and grammatical correctness.
```suggestion
            // If the runtime type view is equal, then the types are considered equal
```
